findings.claim: The 'Interpreting Rate Graphs' collapsible is wrapped in a higher-only block, so Foundation students never see it.
findings.truth: Nothing in the box is Higher tier. Spec 4.6.1.1 lists 'draw, and interpret, graphs showing the quantity of product formed or quantity of reactant used up against time' and 'draw tangents to the curves on these graphs and use the slope of the tangent as a measure of the rate of reaction' with no tier flag. Only 'calculate the gradient of a tangent to the curve on these graphs as a measure of rate of reaction at a specific time' is (HT only), and the box does no calculation. The wrapper is removed; the collapsible, its narration block and the div count are unchanged.

findings.claim: Flashcard answer: 'Endothermic, releasing the same amount of energy.'
findings.truth: An endothermic reaction takes energy in; releasing energy is the definition of exothermic. The card teaches the exothermic/endothermic misconception in the same breath as naming it. The reverse reaction absorbs the same amount of energy that the exothermic forward reaction gives out.
findings.evidence: spec 4.6.2.2: 'If a reversible reaction is exothermic in one direction, it is endothermic in the opposite direction. The same amount of energy is transferred in each case.'

findings.claim: The Haber process box (equation, iron catalyst, about 450 degC, about 200 atmospheres) sits inside the same higher-only wrapper as the Le Chatelier material, so a Foundation student cannot see it.
findings.truth: On separate Chemistry the Haber process is core, untiered content: spec 4.10.4.1 states the raw materials, the iron catalyst, the temperature and the pressure with no tier flag. Only the four bullets about interpreting rate/yield graphs and the equilibrium trade-off are (HT only). The wrapper is closed after the Le Chatelier key fact so the Haber box is visible to both tiers; the Le Chatelier collapsible stays gated. Values check out against the spec.
findings.evidence: spec 4.10.4.1 (untiered lead-in, '(HT only) Students should be able to:' bullets after it); 4.6.2.4-4.6.2.7 each headed (HT only)

findings.claim: Le Chatelier and equilibrium-shift material is gated higher-only in the article, but four practice questions, three knowledge checks and five flashcards on the same material carry no tier flag on a lesson whose tier is 'both'.
findings.truth: Spec 4.6.2.4 to 4.6.2.7 (effect of changing conditions, of concentration, of temperature and of pressure on equilibrium) are each headed (HT only), and the Haber rate/yield trade-off is an (HT only) bullet in 4.10.4.1. Twelve items are prefixed '(Higher tier)', matching the ruling already applied to the sibling science-aqa / chemistry-paper-2 unit. The two Haber recall items (iron catalyst; the equation) are left unflagged because 4.10.4.1 is untiered.

findings.claim: A collapsible on catalytic converters (with the equation 2CO + 2NO -> 2CO2 + N2) and flue gas desulfurisation, reinforced by a key fact, a takeaway, a knowledge check and a 4-mark practice question, all presented as examinable.
findings.truth: Neither process is in the specification: 'catalytic converter' and 'desulfurisation' return no match anywhere in it. Spec 4.9.3.2 stops at the properties and effects of the pollutants themselves. The chemistry is sound (2CO + 2NO -> 2CO2 + N2 balances; FGD with calcium oxide or calcium carbonate does yield calcium sulfate for plaster), so the box is kept and labelled as background rather than deleted. Tom may want to retire practice question 4 and knowledge check 2, which test the same off-spec recall.
findings.evidence: spec 4.9.3.1-4.9.3.2; grep 'catalytic converter' and 'desulfurisation' over the spec returns nothing

findings.claim: Potable water treatment is taught as an ordered list: 'Filtration - passing through filter beds to remove large debris, gravel and sand', then 'Sedimentation - allowing fine particles to settle out', then sterilisation. The same order is repeated in the key fact, in the takeaways and in a flashcard.
findings.truth: Two errors. First, filter beds are built from layers of sand and gravel; they trap insoluble solids and do not remove the sand and gravel. Second, sedimentation precedes filtration in water treatment, so the sequence is inverted in all four places. Spec 4.10.1.2 names choosing a fresh water source, passing the water through filter beds and sterilising; sedimentation is a sewage-treatment step (4.10.1.3) and is harmless as extra detail once it is in the right place. Fixed in the list, the key fact, the takeaway and the flashcard.

findings.claim: The unit has seven lessons, built from the Combined Science lessons, and covers 4.6, 4.7.1, 4.8.1, 4.8.2, 4.9 and 4.10.1-4.10.2 only.
findings.truth: Separate Chemistry Paper 2 content that has no lesson here: 4.7.2.2-4.7.2.4 reactions of alkenes beyond bromine water, alcohols and carboxylic acids (chemistry only); 4.7.3.1-4.7.3.4 addition polymerisation, condensation polymerisation (HT only), amino acids and DNA/natural polymers; the whole of 4.8.3 identification of ions (flame tests, metal hydroxide precipitates, carbonates, halides, sulfates, instrumental methods, flame emission spectroscopy) plus required practical 7, which is Chemistry only; 4.10.1.4 alternative methods of extracting metals (HT only, phytomining and bioleaching); 4.10.3 corrosion and its prevention, alloys, and ceramics/polymers/composites (chemistry only); 4.10.4.2 NPK fertilisers. That is roughly a third of the paper. The sibling science-aqa / chemistry-paper-2 unit carries lessons 8-11 covering exactly this material, labelled 'Separate Chemistry only' where it sits outside Trilogy. Options: port those four lessons here as lessons 8-11 (they were built and fact-checked for the same board), or commission fresh lessons. Recommendation: port them, then add the missing 4.10.1.4 and NPK gaps, since this is the qualification the content actually belongs to. Not editable as a text fix.
findings.evidence: spec 4.7.2, 4.7.3, 4.8.3, 4.10.1.4, 4.10.3, 4.10.4.2; spec 8.2 note 'Practicals 2 and 7 are GCSE Chemistry only'

findings.claim: No required practical is named anywhere in the unit.
findings.truth: Chemistry 8462 Paper 2 carries four required practicals: 5 (how changes in concentration affect rates, by gas volume and by colour change or turbidity), 6 (paper chromatography and Rf values), 7 (chemical tests to identify the ions in unknown single ionic compounds) and 8 (analysis and purification of water samples, including pH, dissolved solids and distillation). Lessons 1, 4 and 7 teach the science of 5, 6 and 8 but never name the practical, so students cannot recognise a required-practical question. Practical 7 has no lesson at all (see F7). No renumbering error to correct, because no numbers are stated.

findings.claim: The two Key Fact boxes carry each other's data-revision-tip prompts: the purity box is prompted with 'recall the four gas tests', and the gas-test box is prompted with 'explain why pure substances have sharp melting points'.
findings.truth: The two prompts are swapped and should be exchanged. Not edited here because the raw dump truncates both attribute values, so no safe find string could be built. A one-line swap in the editor fixes it. Same defect as F10 in the sibling science-aqa unit.
findings.evidence: lesson 4 content_html, data-revision-tip on the n3 and n12 key-fact blocks

findings.claim: Chromatography is explained only as 'different substances travel different distances depending on their solubility'.
findings.truth: The spec requires the stationary phase and mobile phase idea: separation depends on the distribution of a substance between the two phases, not on solubility alone. An answer naming only solubility can lose the second explanation mark. Worth one added sentence, but nothing in the lesson is false.
findings.evidence: spec 4.8.1.3: 'Chromatography involves a stationary phase and a mobile phase. Separation depends on the distribution of substances between the phases.'

summary: Seven lessons checked against AQA Chemistry 8462. One hard error: a lesson 2 flashcard defining the endothermic reverse reaction as releasing energy. Three tier faults: rate-graph interpretation and the whole Haber process box are gated Higher although both are untiered in 8462, while twelve Higher-only equilibrium questions, checks and flashcards carried no tier flag. Lesson 7 inverted the water-treatment sequence and had filter beds removing the sand and gravel they are made of. Lesson 6 teaches catalytic converters and flue gas desulfurisation, neither of which appears in the spec; the chemistry is right so the box is labelled rather than cut. Every other worked example, equation and answer key recomputed clean, including all 35 knowledge checks and the Rf calculation (5.6 / 8.0 = 0.70). The unit-level gap is the real finding: built from the Combined lessons, it omits about a third of separate Chemistry Paper 2 (alcohols, carboxylic acids, polymerisation, the whole of ion identification with required practical 7, corrosion, alloys, composites and NPK fertilisers).
